result.title: ProSE: Probing Reconstruction Error for Semantic-guided Expert Skipping in MoE-MLLMs
result.summary: Mixture-of-Experts Multimodal Large Language Models (MoE-MLLMs) offer scalable inference through sparse expert activation, yet substantial computational redundancy remains among the activated experts. Existing expert skipping methods typically calibrate thresholds based on target skipping ratios or final-output divergence, overlooking the accumulation of skipping-induced error across layers and the varying semantic importance of individual tokens. To address that, we propose ProSE, a training-free, semantic-guided expert skipping framework that probes layer-wise reconstruction error to promote representation consistency compared with default activation. Specifically, we construct query-aware semantic masks to identify salient visual tokens and progressively calibrate modality-specific skipping thresholds for each MoE layer. By minimizing masked reconstruction error under a given budget, ProSE maintains semantic consistency after skipping and allows adaptive expert allocation under limited activation budgets. Extensive experiments on 9 benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements on average over existing expert skipping methods, particularly under aggressive skipping settings. ProSE maintains over 96\% performance on KimiVL-A3B-Inst with 83\% expert skipping and accelerates prefilling by $1.7\times$.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 ProSE，一个免训练、语义引导的 MoE-MLLM 专家跳过框架：用 query-aware 语义掩码标出关键视觉 token，并以逐层掩码重构误差最小化来校准各层的跳过阈值，在给定激活预算下保持表示一致性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其以重构误差探测跳过后的表示一致性、按语义重要性筛选视觉 token 并在预算内分配计算，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与动态计算成本权衡提供可核查线索；但该工作面向推理加速，不涉及推理期 latent 状态生成，迁移需自行设计。
